# Overview

This article plots raw PEEL-1 coverage for thirteen *C. elegans* strains over
the same chromosome-I window.  The bundled fixture contains thirteen BigWig
files and a WS285 GTF subset for the four genes in the interval, so the
workflow is self-contained and does not refer to source BAMs or other external
paths.

The fixture BigWigs were made from one-base bins of the source BAMs without
normalization.  The plotted scores remain raw depth: `geom_coverage()` neither
normalizes, smooths, thresholds, nor expands the stored intervals to one row
per base.

The `rtracklayer` BigWig backend is unsupported on Windows. The code below is
shown on every platform and executed only on macOS and Linux. Windows readers
can view the rendered figure in the
[online tutorial](https://dongyaoliu.github.io/ggexon/articles/bigwig-coverage-demo.html).

```{r peel1-raw-coverage, eval = .Platform$OS.type != "windows", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.alt = "A ggexon plot with thirteen separate PEEL-1 raw-coverage panels in the approved strain order above one centered four-gene annotation panel over the same chromosome-I interval. Every coverage panel places its span-weighted median depth at 85 percent of the panel height, with higher peaks clipped at the panel boundary.", fig.cap = "Raw, unnormalized PEEL-1 coverage for thirteen C. elegans strains over chromosome I:2,332,338-2,373,985. In each independent coverage panel, the span-weighted median depth occupies 85 percent of the panel height. Higher peaks are clipped in the view only; raw BigWig values remain unchanged."}
library(ggexon)

fixture_dir <- system.file("extdata", "peel1_coverage", package = "ggexon")
if (!nzchar(fixture_dir)) {
  fixture_dir <- file.path(
    dirname(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE))),
    "inst", "extdata", "peel1_coverage"
  )
}
gtf <- file.path(
  fixture_dir,
  "WS285.ugt31-zeel1-peel1-nekl1.gtf"
)
strains <- c(
  "XZ1516", "ECA2091", "ECA2199", "ECA369", "QX1791",
  "ECA701", "ECA1769", "ECA2191", "ECA2195", "XZ2211",
  "MY10", "EG4349", "NIC256"
)

coverage_species <- SynSpecies(name = "PEEL-1 raw coverage")
for (strain in strains) {
  individual <- SynIndividual(
    annotation_file = gtf,
    annotation_format = "gtf",
    id = strain
  )
  individual <- add_annotation(
    individual,
    SynBigWigAnnotation(
      name = "coverage",
      bigwig_file = file.path(fixture_dir, paste0(strain, ".raw.bw")),
      metadata = list(signal_unit = "raw_depth")
    )
  )
  coverage_species <- add_individual(coverage_species, individual)
}

coverage_plot <- ggexon(coverage_species) +
  geom_coverage(annotation = "coverage", fill = "#4C78A8") +
  geom_exon(
    species = "XZ1516",
    chr = "I",
    subset = c(2332338L, 2373985L),
    annotation_type = "exon"
  ) +
  facet_genomics(
    ggplot2::vars(track),
    ncol = 1,
    strip.position = "left"
  ) +
  scale_panel_coverage("free_y", auto = TRUE) +
  center_panel_annotation() +
  theme_ggexon_track() +
  theme_ggexon_side_strips("left")
coverage_plot
```

# Reading the tracks

The BigWig values are raw, nonnegative depth. Each file owns a first-class
coverage panel, and `scale_panel_coverage("free_y", auto = TRUE)` gives every
strain its own automatic depth scale. For each panel, ggexon calculates the
span-weighted median coverage value from the rendered BigWig intervals and
places it at 85 percent of the panel height. Roughly half the rendered genomic
span therefore reaches or exceeds that height; tied depth values can make the
fraction differ from exactly 50 percent. Higher peaks are clipped at the panel
boundary without changing the raw BigWig scores or built coverage data. The
calculation uses interval widths directly and does not expand coverage to one
row per base.

The single `geom_exon()` request uses XZ1516 as the representative gene model
for the common chromosome-I window.  It occupies one independent annotation
panel below the thirteen coverage panels; `center_panel_annotation()` centers that
gene model within its panel without changing annotation data or any coverage
scale.  No synthetic negative annotation band is added to a coverage panel.

# Compress introns

Add the genomic scale to align every coverage track with the representative
gene model while shortening introns:

```{r peel1-compressed-grammar, eval=FALSE}
coverage_plot + scale_x_ggexon_genomic(intron_factor = 10)
```

`geom_coverage()` automatically splits intervals at exon/intron scale boundaries.
The build first trains the map from exon layers, then applies it to related
panels and layers. Coverage and other annotations do not redefine that map.
Depths and genomic-width weights for automatic y limits remain unchanged;
only horizontal distances change. Built data retain the parent interval in
`interval_start`/`interval_end` and each piece's original rectangle edges in
`genomic_edge_start`/`genomic_edge_end`. Coverage needs an exon-style annotation
source to define the map; `strip_scale_x()` remains unsupported.

For reproducibility, `manifest.tsv` in the fixture directory records each
source BAM, output file, interval, bin size, normalization setting, and
checksum.  The BAM files themselves are not distributed with the package.
